newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Seven killed in election day violence in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed in election day violence in Pakistan.

text.p: Seven people were killed in two separate incidents on Monday as Pakistanis voted to choose a new National Assembly, although officials said that generally polling was peaceful.
Five people were shot dead when two groups clashed over a land dispute near a polling station in Gujranwala in the central province of Punjab, police said.

In the southern city of Karachi, where hundreds have died in factional feuding in recent years, two supporters of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) were killed, MQM sources and ambulance workers said.

MQM spokesman Kunwar Khalid Younus said polling agent Mohammad Hanif died in hospital after being kidnapped and tortured by unidentified gunmen. He was the brother of an MQM candidate for the Sindh Provincial Assembly. Each party nominates agents to observe voting at each polling station.
Younus said gunmen also killed another MQM sympathiser in the eastern Al-Flaha Society district.
Hundreds of people have died in feuding between MQM factions in the past four years. The MQM speaks for Urdu-speakers who migrated to Pakistan from India in 1947 and their descendants.

The MQM and the breakaway MQM-Haqiqi faction traded charges of harassment and the MQM-Haqiqi eventually said it was boycotting the last hour of polling. The faction had not been expected to gain any seats.

Monday's elections followed President Farooq Leghari's removal of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto on November 5. Leghari accused her government of corruption, nepotism and extra-judicial killings in Karachi and the Supreme Court ruled last week that the president's action had been justified.
